A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTAug/TTAdapt research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across nine benchmarks, method ablations, computational measurements, cross-model experiments, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds comparison results and statistical uncertainty reporting.

M1.justification: Token-level aggregation, greedy decoding, pseudolabel-based adaptation, and resetting weights between questions remain unchanged. The new Algorithm 1 formalizes the existing TTAdapt procedure; Appendix I retains the implementation and optimization settings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine benchmarks covering VQA, multiple-choice questions, yes/no questions, and captioning, with the same model coverage. The new comparison uses existing benchmarks; Appendix J's added selection rationale does not change the evaluated data.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 expands the temperature-sampling comparison to include Sample-and-Rank and Self-Synthesizer alongside Self-Consistency and Self-Selector. The first two were already evaluated with input perturbations in v1 Table 2, retained as v2 Table 3; no new baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: New Section 4.1 compares eight sampled candidates per comparator with eight augmented TTAug inputs and reports runtime and generated-token counts. Appendix J.2 replaces the previously stated TextVQA scoring formula with leave-one-annotator-out averaging. This changes the documented protocol without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The text-augmentation ablation revises its evidence for self-paraphrasing on GQA from 10.0 to 0.0, indicating no improvement there over the baseline. Its design is unchanged. Other augmentation, aggregation, layer, modality, and adaptation analyses and the qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without corresponding standard errors. New Appendix K systematically supplies standard errors for benchmark scores in all main-text tables, using empirical per-sample variance divided by sample count. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, but does not establish repeated runs, seed robustness, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds temperature-sampling results for Sample-and-Rank and Self-Synthesizer, with means of 41.0 and 43.9, plus comparator runtimes and generated-token counts. These are additional settings, not improvements over their retained input-perturbation results. Self-paraphrasing's GQA score changes from 10.0 in v1 Table 3 to 0.0 in v2 Table 4; other matched scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix J.2 changes Equation 5 mathematically by averaging capped agreement scores over leave-one-out annotator subsets instead of using the full answer set once. The theoretical analyses, assumptions, theorem, and proof in Appendices A and B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about two efficient scaling methods, token-level aggregation, source-free adaptation, and generalization across models. The added evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.8 more explicitly discusses limits to universal hyperparameters and connects transfer to similarity with the tuning model. Appendix E adds claims that A100-derived resource trade-offs transfer across hardware, without additional hardware experiments. Appendix J newly explains benchmark exclusions and the preference for objective evaluation.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 explicitly documents TTAdapt's supervision objective, update loop, final generation, and reset. Appendix E clarifies that KV caching accelerates sequential generation rather than being required for correctness, and discusses operation without caching. Existing detailed hyperparameters, prompts, libraries, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning relative to earlier augmentation and adaptation research are retained. Baseline descriptions are relocated without introducing new cited methods.

P1.justification: v2 introduces a comparison subsection before the existing design analyses, consolidates baseline descriptions there, adds a standard-error appendix, and relabels the qualitative appendix from K to L. Local explanations, terminology capitalization, and publication headers change, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Results presentation expands systematically through paired mean and standard-error panels for every main-text accuracy comparison in Tables 11–16. These redisplay existing means alongside new uncertainty information. v2 also adds the accuracy/runtime/token comparison table and Algorithm 1; existing figures and qualitative panels retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through systematic standard errors, a direct accuracy/cost comparison, and clearer algorithm documentation. The revised GQA entry now agrees with its reported mean, resolving an internal inconsistency. These gains are limited by the largely unchanged experimental foundation: uncertainty concerns test samples rather than repeated runs, and the stronger hardware-transfer assurances remain supported only by A100 measurements.
